subject: Action plan: private cutover & control plane compatibility (next tests)
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Alex Moreno <alex@datafoundry.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 15 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Action plan: private cutover & control plane compatibility (next tests)

Hi Alex — thanks again for taking the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single playbook to run against the DataFoundry environment.

Recap (high level):
- Primary ask: confirm feasibility of migrating inference traffic to a private/VPC deployment while keeping the Redwood control plane reachable in a secure, auditable manner.
- Main constraints: strict egress controls, air-gap windows during cutover, and vendor procurement windows in late Q3.

Proposed immediate tests (priority order):
1) Control-plane reachability test (proxy-only): set up a one-hour scheduled window where DF allows egress to a narrow set of Redwood control-plane endpoints through a customer-managed proxy. Objective: confirm TLS handshake, mTLS if required, and token-based provisioning. Expected outcome: list of IPs/ports + any TLS negotiation issues.
2) KV-cache persistence smoke test: run a short workload (500 short requests) to validate checkpointing and cold-start latency for model cache warmup under the private runtime.
3) Air-gap dry-run: simulate a 30-minute cutover in an isolated subnet with no outbound internet except to the proxy; verify model loads and fallback behaviors.

Owners & timing:
- Redwood: Karthik (tech lead) + Ben (SE) to run tests and collect logs.
- DataFoundry: Alex to schedule firewall/proxy windows and provide the network diagram + temporary egress ACLs.
- Target: complete tests the week of Aug 24 if DF can confirm windows this week.

Deliverables we will produce:
- Runbook for each test (checklist, expected artifacts) — attached draft (redwood-controlplane-proxy-checklist.md).
- Capture of control-plane traces and connection logs for DF to review.
- Post-test readout and next-step recommendation (quantified latency/cost delta vs. hyperscaler).

Questions for you before we lock dates:
- Can you share a current network diagram with NAT/proxy details (requesting DF v2 if available)?
- Any org-level constraints on scheduling cutover windows (maintenance windows, procurement freeze weeks)?

I attached our draft checklist and included a short timeline suggestion below. If that looks good I'll coordinate directly with Karthik and Ben to book times.

Thanks —
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jordan_blake@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0132

Jordan — thanks for the clear breakdown. We're keen to move quickly. A few quick notes: we can open a 2-hour maintenance window on Aug 25 between 02:00-04:00 UTC for the proxy test (internal ops prefers that slot).

I attached our latest network diagram (df-private-network-diagram-v2.pdf) — it shows our egress proxies and private peering to HyperscaleCorp in the "Edge" VPC. A couple of asks from our side:
- We need a list of exact IPs/DNS hostnames Redwood will call from the control plane during the proxy test.
- Can Redwood provide guidance on whether mTLS is supported or if we should expect bearer-token-only flows?

Procurement looped in for any SOW / scoping questions — they asked for a short SOW that lists the tests and expected deliverables. We can start with a 1-page SOW if that helps speed approval.

Alex Moreno

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 17 Aug 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Action plan: private cutover & control plane compatibility (next tests)

Jordan / Marissa — wrote up a short technical runbook and a set of validation criteria attached to this thread. Highlights:
- Control-plane proxy test steps:
  1) Provide DF with temporary tokens (scoped) and a small verification endpoint that performs a single provisioning handshake.
  2) Validate TLS ciphers and observe ClientHello/ServerHello — flag any TLS 1.2-only proxies.
  3) If DF requires mTLS, we will run an mTLS handshake test using a short-lived cert bundle (we'll need cert distribution instructions).
- KV-cache persistence: we instrument a 2-minute workload that exercises model cache fill + eviction; capture per-token latencies and cache hit ratio.
- Air-gap dry-run: disable outbound DNS and enforce egress ACLs; monitor for dependency failures (e.g., license check endpoints).

I attached the control-plane checklist (redwood-controlplane-proxy-checklist.md) — it's intentionally minimal so DF can annotate. Ben — can you confirm SE availability for Aug 25 02:00-04:00 UTC?

Karthik
Sr. Staff Engineer, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com

I'll schedule a short sync for Aug 20 (30 minutes) to align on the SOW and test checklist. If procurement needs a more formal SOW we can expand, but the one-pager should unblock approvals.

Thanks everyone — looking forward to the dry-run.
